name: app/money
title: Money
summary: An amount of money formatted for a locale, from integer minor units and an ISO 4217 code, inside a <data> element whose value is the exact decimal. No default currency and no default locale: the caller passes both.

props.name: amountMinor
props.description: The amount in the currency's minor unit, as an integer (1250 is 12.50 USD; 1235 is ¥1,235).

props.name: currency
props.description: An ISO 4217 code, three capital letters ("USD", "ZWG", "ZAR", "KES"). Required: there is no default. Anything else is refused with a RangeError.

props.name: locale
props.description: A BCP 47 locale ("en-ZW", "fr-SN"). Required: there is no default.

props.name: display
props.description: How the currency is shown (Intl's currencyDisplay).

behaviour: The text is `Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: "currency", currency })` with the currency's own minor-unit digits (2 for USD, 0 for JPY, 3 for KWD).
The amount is placed from the integer as an exact decimal string, never through a float, so large amounts and negative amounts are exact.
The root is <data value="<exact decimal>" data-currency="<code>">, so a machine reads the amount without parsing the text.
There is no default currency and no default locale. A currency that is not three capital letters, or an amount that is not an integer, is refused (RangeError) rather than shown wrongly.
The formatting is `formatMoney` / `moneyValue` from the framework-free `money` module, which servers and other components share.

zero-digit.description: A currency with no minor unit.

three-digit.description: A currency with three minor digits, shown by code.

negative.description: A refund: a negative amount, exact.

aria: The formatted text is the accessible text.

theming.brandOverlay: None: it inherits its colour and size from where it is placed.

responsive: Inline text; tabular figures so amounts line up in a column.
contract:
contract
  slot is "money"
  when default shows data "12.50"
  when zero-digit shows data "1,235"
end

checks.say: The exact decimal and the code are machine-readable.
A zero-digit currency has no decimals.
Zimbabwe Gold is formatted by its code.
